newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends stronger on U.S. report.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends stronger on U.S. report.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed stronger at C$1.3834 (US$0.7229) in moderate trade on Thursday on the back of U.S. economic data in the morning. * Traders said markets viewed the data as a sign that the Fed may not raise interest rates at its July meeting. * The unit bounced back from midday highs after failing to sustain a break through C$1.3810 (US$0.7241).
Canada's dollar closed stronger in moderate trading on Thursday, firming to C$1.3834 (US$0.7229) from its open at C$1.3873 (US$0.7208).

The currency strengthened after a tame U.S. retail sales report reduced expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike interest rates when its Open Market Committee meets in July, traders said.

"The whole thing was on the retail sales number out of the U.S. The bond market loved it. It was basically buy Canada on the news. We brought it down but ran into some strong resistance at the (C$1.38)05-10 area," one dealer said.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets and the Canadian dollar strengthened after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that retail sales fell 0.1 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.4 percent rise.
Analysts said the increased expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in July takes pressure off the Bank of Canada and the Canadian dollar.
The currency had been under pressure from concerns that the Bank of Canada might hold domestic rates steady even as U.S. rates rose, drawing capital flows out of the country.
Analysts said the market was now looking ahead to U.S. producer price index data for May being released on Friday for confirmation that U.S. price pressures remained subdued.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 82.55 yen from Wednesday's 80.17 yen and jumped to 1.2497 marks from Wednesday's 1.2372 marks.
